sources.entry: PHP: _Build And Learn Git With PHP_

summary.title: Build And Learn Git With PHP
summary.one_liner: You learn how Git works internally by implementing core Git commands (init, hash-object, cat-file, write-tree, ls-tree, add, ls-files, commit, log) yourself in PHP.
takeaways: Git's core behavior can be understood by reimplementing its plumbing commands.
The tutorial covers init, hash-object, cat-file, write-tree, ls-tree, add, ls-files, commit and log.
Basic familiarity with everyday Git commands and concepts is helpful before starting.
Attempting the commands yourself first is encouraged; the early ones are the hardest.
summary.summary: This introductory page opens a tutorial that teaches how Git works internally by having the reader implement a set of Git commands in PHP. The listed commands are init, hash-object, cat-file, write-tree, ls-tree, add, ls-files, commit and log. The author says each command and its function is explained as the reader goes, and recommends trying to build them independently first. The page itself is only an introduction, so the implementation details are not present here.
